messages:
elaine: Heads-up — customer on private deployment reported missing audit entries for KMS decrypts after our RBAC tweak last night. Noticed spikes in `kms-proxy` restarts in their logs. Anyone seen this pattern before?

samir: Oof. Do we have a pointer to the crash logs? could be token exchange failing if RBAC removed the serviceaccount permission to hit the keystore.

elaine: pasted the snippet from their agent: `2026-03-15T09:12:03Z kms-proxy tls handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate` then `permission denied: audit.log.write`.

maria: That `bad certificate` + `audit.log.write` combo screams: proxy can't reach KMS CA endpoint because netpol blocked egress, then fallback to local signing failed after RBAC change. Also there's a known agent CVE (AGENT-2026-042) that causes noisy restarts when certs are rotated.

samir: Can we confirm netpol? ask customer to run `kubectl get networkpolicy -n redwood -o yaml` or just `kubectl describe np` for the nodes holding secret-sync. If they accidentally narrowed egress to `10.0.0.0/8` only, they could block the KMS IPs.

jun: Sharing a minimal egress-allow netpol we use in canary — might help them test quickly:```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-kms-egress
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kms-proxy
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 52.45.12.0/24   # example KMS range
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

jun: (note: prefer IP block for private deployments where DNS is restricted)

elaine: thanks. customer also mentioned they applied a tighter RBAC role for `redwood-audit-writer` which removed `create` on `events` in the audit namespace. Could be two correlated changes.

maria: action: check agent version first. run `kubectl -n redwood get ds/agent -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'` and compare to patched build (>= v1.4.7). if vulnerable, upgrade asap — it kills log flush on cert rotation.

samir: also validate conntrack/nat table. saw a case where high conntrack dropped tls handshakes intermittently. `ss -s` on the node and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` are quick checks.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment triggered: redwood/kms-proxy v2.1.4 -> v2.1.5 on canary nodes (canary-3). Monitor logs for TLS handshake errors for 15m. :rocket:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-03 created by elaine for 'priv-deploy audit/KMS gaps'. Priority: P2.

elaine: Proposed next steps for customer: 1) Temporarily apply `allow-kms-egress` netpol snippet 2) revert RBAC change for `redwood-audit-writer` (or add `create` on `events`) 3) confirm agent image version and upgrade if < v1.4.7 4) provide `kubectl logs` of `kms-proxy` for last 2 hours and `kubectl describe pod` for one failing pod.

maria: I'll own triage for CVE and post a mitigation doc in the incident ticket. samir can you add conntrack checks to the troubleshooting checklist?

samir: yup will add. also recommend they enable short-lived mTLS between proxy and KMS (identity-based) not IP allowlists as a follow-up.

jun: one more quick hardening note: when we open egress for KMS, scope it to specific serviceaccount + namespace and logflows. do NOT open cluster-wide egress except for a narrow CIDR.

elaine: perfect. pinging customer with steps. will update INC-2026-03 with results. thanks team :thumbsup:
